scope: Focused review of independent two-sided scale-anchor candidates in Europe/North Atlantic for the 1337 model.
selection_rule: A candidate can supervise global scale only with a same-boundary population interval, independent local-food pressure evidence, a defensible saturation/capacity upper bound, >=95% EU5 crosswalk coverage, and no dominant imported-food or city/trade-hub semantics.

candidate_dispositions.reason: Stable population and Sheep Letter pasture rules do not establish an upper human equilibrium; staple grain imports break the local-food requirement.
Partial 1469 hearth extrapolation, 20% loss assumption, urban population share and commercial/regional grain dependence prevent a two-sided intrinsic-capacity interval.
Both county estimates are conditional on England's assumed 4.0m total and share the existing England source family; they cannot add independent scale information.
Florence and other city-states imported grain from long distances; city/country population and contado boundaries are not intrinsic local-food observations.
Already promoted; this wave did not count it as a new independent family.
Already promoted; this wave did not count a duplicate Iceland model as a new independent family.

conclusion: No new independent two-sided scale anchor met the strict gate. The wave adds auditable European validation groups and explicit rejection reasons while preserving the existing Artois and Iceland anchors. Training must not treat the new packets as scale targets.
